# **Don’t rage against the machines**

India’s Navratri festival is ten days of fasting, music, dance and prayer, all in celebration of the ten-armed Hindu Goddess Durga, who famously defeated the demon king Mahishasura in battle.

Depending on regional tradition, each day of the festival is dedicated to a different subject of devotion. In South India, for example, Day One honors the Earth and foundational wisdom, with devotees ritually planting sprouts in a bed of sacred soil. Day Two honors discipline and penance with strict fasts and quiet prayer.

Day Nine honors tools.

The ninth day of the Navratri festival — today! — is known in South India as “Ayudha Puja”: the “worship of tools and instruments.”

The ancient tradition began with the warrior class honoring the tools of its trade — swords, daggers, bows and arrows — in remembrance of the ten divine weapons Durga wielded (one in each hand!) to defeat Mahishasura.

Today, it’s tools of all trades. Farm equipment, construction machinery, kitchen utensils, office computers — on the ninth day of Navratri, anything that helps people do their jobs is honored with ritual cleaning, decorations, blessings, and a day of rest.

Mechanics wash their tools with the same care a priest washes an idol. Engineers garland their laptops with a necklace of flowers. Machinists bow with folded hands before their lathes and drills.
